claim: The use of a chromatin donor template instead of a naked DNA donor template increases the efficiency of homology-directed repair (HDR) in cells.
source: Here we describe a strategy for increasing the efficiency of HDR in cells by using a chromatin donor template instead of a naked DNA donor template.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing increased HDR efficiency with chromatin templates.

claim: The use of chromatin donor templates increases the frequency of HDR-edited clones.
source: The use of chromatin, which is the natural form of DNA in the nucleus, increases the frequency of HDR-edited clones as well as homozygous editing.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing increased percentages of GFP-positive cells with chromatin templates.

claim: The use of chromatin donor templates increases the frequency of homozygous editing.
source: The use of chromatin, which is the natural form of DNA in the nucleus, increases the frequency of HDR-edited clones as well as homozygous editing.
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis data showing higher percentages of homozygous clones with chromatin templates.

claim: Transfection of chromatin results in negligible cytotoxicity.
source: In addition, transfection of chromatin results in negligible cytotoxicity.
evidence: This is supported by cell viability data presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: A chromatin donor template should be useful for the precise insertion or replacement of DNA fragments that contain the coding regions of genes.
source: These findings suggest that a chromatin donor template should be useful for a wide range of HDR applications such as the precise insertion or replacement of DNA fragments that contain the coding regions of genes.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results showing enhanced HDR efficiency with chromatin templates.

claim: HDR typically involves the generation of a specifically targeted DNA double-strand break (DSB) in the presence of a homologous DNA donor template.
source: For genome engineering in cells, HDR typically involves the generation of a specifically targeted DNA double-strand break (DSB) in the presence of a homologous DNA donor template that contains the desired sequence to be modified or inserted (Urnov et al., 2005; Bedell et al., 2012; Jinek et al., 2012; Cong et al., 2013; Pickar-Oliver and Gersbach, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by multiple citations.

claim: A key challenge in successful genome editing has been the low efficiency of HDR.
source: A key challenge in successful genome editing has been the low efficiency of HDR (Carroll, 2014; Harrison et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Base editing and prime editing are highly effective for generating specific alterations in short stretches of DNA (<50 nt).
source: For the generation of specific alterations in a short stretch of DNA (<50 nt), recently developed techniques such as base editing (Rees and Liu, 2018; Molla and Yang, 2019) and prime editing (Anzalone et al., 2019) have been shown to be highly effective.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work on these techniques.

claim: Base editing and prime editing cannot be used for the precise insertion or replacement of >50 bp DNA fragments.
source: These powerful methods cannot, however, be used for the precise insertion or replacement of >50 bp DNA fragments, such as those containing the coding regions of genes.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the limitations of these techniques.

claim: Homologous strand pairing occurs more efficiently with a chromatin donor template than with a naked DNA donor template in vitro.
source: Based on our previous observation that homologous strand pairing, an early step in HDR, occurs more efficiently with a chromatin donor template than with a plain (naked) DNA donor template in vitro (Alexiadis and Kadonaga, 2002), we postulated that HDR in cells might similarly be more efficient with a chromatin relative to a naked DNA donor template.
evidence: This is based on a previous publication by the authors.

claim: The use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 7.4-fold increase in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the GAPDH locus in MCF10A cells.
source: we observed that the use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 7.4-, 2.9-, and 2.3-fold increase (average of three biological replicates) in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the GAPDH, RAB11A, and ACTB loci, respectively (Figures 1B, C and D and Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from three biological replicates.

claim: The use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 2.9-fold increase in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the RAB11A locus in MCF10A cells.
source: we observed that the use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 7.4-, 2.9-, and 2.3-fold increase (average of three biological replicates) in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the GAPDH, RAB11A, and ACTB loci, respectively (Figures 1B, C and D and Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from three biological replicates.

claim: The use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 2.3-fold increase in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the ACTB locus in MCF10A cells.
source: we observed that the use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 7.4-, 2.9-, and 2.3-fold increase (average of three biological replicates) in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the GAPDH, RAB11A, and ACTB loci, respectively (Figures 1B, C and D and Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from three biological replicates.

claim: The use of chromatin relative to naked DNA donor templates resulted in a 2.1-fold increase in homozygous editing at the GAPDH locus in MCF10A cells.
source: At the GAPDH locus, the use of chromatin relative to naked DNA donor templates resulted in a 2.1-fold increase in homozygous editing.
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis of individual GFP-positive clones.

claim: At the RAB11A locus, there was a high frequency of homozygous insertions with the naked DNA donor template.
source: At the RAB11A locus, there was a high frequency of homozygous insertions with the naked DNA donor template, and the use of a chromatin donor template only slightly augments (1.1-fold increase) the percentage of homozygous clones.
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis data.

claim: The use of a chromatin donor template results in a 1.1-fold increase in the percentage of homozygous clones at the RAB11A locus.
source: At the RAB11A locus, there was a high frequency of homozygous insertions with the naked DNA donor template, and the use of a chromatin donor template only slightly augments (1.1-fold increase) the percentage of homozygous clones.
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis data.

claim: At the ACTB locus, homozygous insertions were observed only with a chromatin donor template.
source: Strikingly, at the ACTB locus, homozygous insertions were observed only with a chromatin donor template.
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis data showing no homozygous clones with DNA templates but 3 homozygous clones with chromatin templates.

claim: The overall efficiency of achieving homozygous editing in diploid MCF10A cells was 15-fold at the GAPDH locus.
source: The overall efficiency of achieving homozygous editing in diploid MCF10A cells was 15-fold (7.4 × 2.1) at the GAPDH locus, 3.2-fold (2.9 × 1.1) at the RAB11A locus, and large but not quantifiable at the ACTB locus, at which we saw homozygous editing only with a chromatin donor template.
evidence: This is calculated from the fold-increases in GFP-positive cells and homozygous editing.

claim: The overall efficiency of achieving homozygous editing in diploid MCF10A cells was 3.2-fold at the RAB11A locus.
source: The overall efficiency of achieving homozygous editing in diploid MCF10A cells was 15-fold (7.4 × 2.1) at the GAPDH locus, 3.2-fold (2.9 × 1.1) at the RAB11A locus, and large but not quantifiable at the ACTB locus, at which we saw homozygous editing only with a chromatin donor template.
evidence: This is calculated from the fold-increases in GFP-positive cells and homozygous editing.

claim: HeLa cells are aneuploid and contain four copies of the GAPDH gene.
source: HeLa cells are aneuploid and contain four copies of the GAPDH gene, which is located on chromosome 12.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HeLa cells.

claim: The GAPDH gene is located on chromosome 12.
source: HeLa cells are aneuploid and contain four copies of the GAPDH gene, which is located on chromosome 12.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genomic location of GAPDH.

claim: The use of a chromatin donor template results in a 2.3-fold increase in the efficiency of insertion of the GFP sequence in at least one GAPDH locus in HeLa cells.
source: we observed that the use of a chromatin donor template results in a 2.3-fold increase (average of three biological replicates) in the efficiency of insertion of the GFP sequence in at least one GAPDH locus in HeLa cells (Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from three biological replicates.

claim: There was a substantial increase (5/18 clones versus 1/21 clones) in the efficiency of formation of homozygous clones with the use of a chromatin donor template instead of a naked DNA donor template in HeLa cells.
source: In this analysis, we found a substantial increase (5/18 clones versus 1/21 clones) in the efficiency of formation of homozygous clones with the use of a chromatin donor template instead of a naked DNA donor template (Figure 3C,D,E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis of individual clones.

claim: At each of the three amounts of donor template tested, there was a higher efficiency of generation of GFP-positive cells with chromatin relative to naked DNA in HeLa cells.
source: At each of the three amounts of donor template, we consistently saw a higher efficiency of generation of GFP-positive cells with chromatin relative to naked DNA.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data at different donor template concentrations.

claim: There was an increase in the fold-enhancement by chromatin as the amount of donor template was increased.
source: Moreover, there was an increase in the fold-enhancement by chromatin as the amount of donor template was increased.
evidence: This is observed from the data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Chromatin is of comparable or lower toxicity to cells relative to naked DNA in transfection experiments.
source: These experiments revealed that chromatin is of comparable or lower toxicity to cells relative to naked DNA in transfection experiments.
evidence: This is supported by cell viability data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Chromatin is the natural form of DNA in the eukaryotic nucleus.
source: We suggest that chromatin, as the natural form of DNA in the eukaryotic nucleus, is the preferred substrate (relative to naked DNA) for the factors that mediate homologous recombination in cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cell biology.

claim: Chromatin is the preferred substrate (relative to naked DNA) for the factors that mediate homologous recombination in cells.
source: We suggest that chromatin, as the natural form of DNA in the eukaryotic nucleus, is the preferred substrate (relative to naked DNA) for the factors that mediate homologous recombination in cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their experimental results.

claim: Eukaryotic Rad51 and Rad54, but not bacterial RecA, can mediate homologous strand pairing with a chromatin donor template.
source: In previous biochemical studies, we and others found that eukaryotic Rad51 and Rad54, but not bacterial RecA, can mediate homologous strand pairing, an early step in HDR, with a chromatin donor template (Alexiadis and Kadonaga, 2002; Jaskelioff et al., 2003).
evidence: This is based on previous published work.

claim: The findings on HDR with chromatin donor templates in cells are consistent with the results of earlier biochemical studies on homologous strand exchange.
source: Hence, the new findings on HDR with chromatin donor templates in cells are consistent with the results of the earlier biochemical studies on homologous strand exchange.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by the authors connecting their current results to previous work.

claim: A common factor in HDR experiments has been the use of a non-chromatin donor template.
source: A common factor in these HDR experiments has been, however, the use of a non-chromatin donor template.
evidence: This is based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: A higher efficiency of HDR with chromatin relative to naked DNA was consistently observed.
source: In these experiments, we consistently observed a higher efficiency of HDR with chromatin relative to naked DNA.
evidence: This is supported by data from multiple experiments at different loci and in different cell lines.

claim: The use of a chromatin donor template instead of a naked DNA donor template would be a broadly useful strategy for the precise insertion or replacement of DNA sequences via HDR with different methods.
source: These findings therefore suggest that the use of a chromatin donor template instead of a naked DNA donor template would be a broadly useful strategy for the precise insertion or replacement of DNA sequences via HDR with different methods.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results.

claim: Transfection of chromatin donor templates does not affect cell viability.
source: Moreover, transfection of chromatin donor templates, which can be simply prepared by salt dialysis methodology with purified DNA and core histones, does not affect cell viability.
evidence: This is supported by cell viability data.

claim: Chromatin donor templates can be simply prepared by salt dialysis methodology with purified DNA and core histones.
source: Moreover, transfection of chromatin donor templates, which can be simply prepared by salt dialysis methodology with purified DNA and core histones, does not affect cell viability.
evidence: This is based on the methods used in the study.

claim: Current methods for HDR can be easily adapted to include chromatin donor templates in place of their naked DNA counterparts.
source: Thus, current methods for HDR can be easily adapted to include chromatin donor templates in place of their naked DNA counterparts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Chromatin was reconstituted by using native core histones from Drosophila embryos.
source: In this regard, it is notable that we reconstituted chromatin by using native core histones from Drosophila embryos.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used.

claim: Core histones from Drosophila embryos contain an undefined broad mixture of covalent histone modifications.
source: These histones contain an undefined broad mixture of covalent histone modifications (Levenstein and Kadonaga, 2002).
evidence: This is based on a previous publication.

claim: Core histones and their modifications are highly conserved throughout eukaryotes.
source: Because the core histones and their modifications are highly conserved throughout eukaryotes, it seems likely that similar results would be obtained with core histones from other sources.
evidence: This is established knowledge in molecular biology.

claim: Similar results would likely be obtained with core histones from other sources.
source: Because the core histones and their modifications are highly conserved throughout eukaryotes, it seems likely that similar results would be obtained with core histones from other sources.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the conservation of histones.

claim: The magnitude of enhancement of HDR by chromatin could be further increased by variation of the core histone sequences and modifications.
source: It is possible, however, that the magnitude of enhancement of HDR by chromatin could be further increased by variation of the core histone sequences and modifications.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future improvements.

claim: There are excellent techniques for the alteration of short (<50 bp) stretches of DNA.
source: In conclusion, although there are excellent techniques for the alteration of short (<50 bp) stretches of DNA (Rees and Liu, 2018; Molla and Yang, 2019; Anzalone et al., 2019), there remains a need for increasing the efficiency of the specific insertion or replacement of longer DNA segments that may contain sequences such as the coding regions of genes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published work.

claim: There remains a need for increasing the efficiency of the specific insertion or replacement of longer DNA segments that may contain sequences such as the coding regions of genes.
source: In conclusion, although there are excellent techniques for the alteration of short (<50 bp) stretches of DNA (Rees and Liu, 2018; Molla and Yang, 2019; Anzalone et al., 2019), there remains a need for increasing the efficiency of the specific insertion or replacement of longer DNA segments that may contain sequences such as the coding regions of genes.
evidence: This is based on the authors' assessment of the field.

claim: Chromatin donor templates might be particularly useful for applications involving the insertion or replacement of longer DNA segments.
source: We anticipate that chromatin donor templates might be particularly useful for such applications.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results.

claim: Many new gene editing techniques will be developed in the future.
source: In addition, we expect that many new gene editing techniques will be developed in the future, and that some of these methods will benefit from the use of chromatin donor templates.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future developments.

claim: Some future gene editing methods will benefit from the use of chromatin donor templates.
source: In addition, we expect that many new gene editing techniques will be developed in the future, and that some of these methods will benefit from the use of chromatin donor templates.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the current findings.

claim: The low toxicity of chromatin to cells may be useful for many current and future methods.
source: Furthermore, the low toxicity of chromatin to cells may be useful for many current and future methods.
evidence: This is based on the cell viability data and is a speculative statement about applications.

claim: MCF10A cells are non-tumorigenic epithelial cells derived from human mammary glands.
source: With standard CRISPR-Cas9 methodology and human MCF10A cells (non-tumorigenic epithelial cells derived from human mammary glands), we observed that the use of a chromatin donor template relative to a naked DNA donor template resulted in a 7.4-, 2.9-, and 2.3-fold increase (average of three biological replicates) in the directed insertion of GFP sequences at the GAPDH, RAB11A, and ACTB loci, respectively (Figures 1B, C and D and Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the MCF10A cell line.

claim: HeLa cells are human cervical adenocarcinoma cells that are widely used in biomedical research.
source: To determine whether a chromatin donor template affects the efficiency of HDR in a different cell line, we examined the insertion of GFP sequences at the GAPDH locus in HeLa cells, which are human cervical adenocarcinoma cells that are widely used in biomedical research.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the HeLa cell line.

claim: MCF10A cells are diploid.
source: Therefore, to test the frequency of occurrence of precise homozygous gene editing in the diploid MCF10A cells, we carried out PCR analyses of the individual GFP-positive clones
evidence: This is established knowledge about MCF10A cells.

claim: Imperfect editing was observed, in which there was at least one improperly edited chromosome.
source: We also observed imperfect editing, in which there was at least one improperly edited chromosome, as indicated by either the absence of an edited chromosome or the presence of a PCR product whose size is not consistent with that of an edited or wild-type chromosome.
evidence: This is supported by PCR analysis data.

claim: Two apparently homozygous clones contained one chromosome with a precisely edited allele and one chromosome with a large deletion at the other allele.
source: In addition, by performing long-range PCR as in Kosicki et al., 2018, we identified two apparently homozygous clones that contained one chromosome with a precisely edited allele and one chromosome with a large deletion at the other allele (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by long-range PCR analysis data.

claim: In the generation of homozygous clones, it is important to carry out both standard and long-range PCR analyses.
source: Hence, in the generation of homozygous clones, it is important to carry out both standard and long-range PCR analyses.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the observation of clones with large deletions.

claim: The ACTB locus serves as an example in which the use of a chromatin template relative to a naked DNA template was the difference between a successful and an unsuccessful HDR experiment.
source: The ACTB locus serves as an example in which the use of a chromatin template relative to a naked DNA template was the difference between a successful and an unsuccessful HDR experiment.
evidence: This is based on the observation that homozygous editing at ACTB was only achieved with chromatin templates.

claim: The chromatin was reconstituted by using salt dialysis methodology with plasmid DNA and purified core histones from Drosophila embryos.
source: The chromatin was reconstituted by using salt dialysis methodology with plasmid DNA and purified core histones from Drosophila embryos, which contain a broad mixture of covalent modifications that have not been precisely resolved (Levenstein and Kadonaga, 2002).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: Core histones from Drosophila embryos contain a broad mixture of covalent modifications that have not been precisely resolved.
source: The chromatin was reconstituted by using salt dialysis methodology with plasmid DNA and purified core histones from Drosophila embryos, which contain a broad mixture of covalent modifications that have not been precisely resolved (Levenstein and Kadonaga, 2002).
evidence: This is based on a previous publication.

claim: The experiments were performed under standard CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing conditions.
source: These experiments were performed under standard CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing conditions, as in Ran et al., 2013.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend and references a published protocol.

claim: At least two biological replicates were performed for each experimental condition.
source: To ensure the reproducibility of the results, at least two biological replicates were performed for each experimental condition.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The precise integration of the GFP sequence at the target sites in representative edited clones was confirmed by DNA sequencing.
source: In addition, the precise integration of the GFP sequence at the target sites in representative edited clones was confirmed by DNA sequencing.
evidence: This describes validation of the experimental results.

claim: The DNA sequences of three GAPDH clones and three ACTB clones were determined across the insertion junctions and the GFP sequences were precisely inserted into the target sites in all six clones.
source: To confirm the integrity of the homozygous clones obtained with chromatin donor templates, we determined the DNA sequences of three GAPDH clones and three ACTB clones across the insertion junctions and found that the GFP sequences were precisely inserted into the target sites in all six clones.
evidence: This is supported by DNA sequencing data.
